about: Pagination and date-window scenarios (appendix A 23, 24, 26, 26b, 30). Each scenario serves pages in order: groups of records (only the fields the policy reads: id, created_at UTC, pinned, unavailable) with has_next and cursor, or an error (failed | shape_changed | checkpoint | rate_limit | login | budget). options: limit, since/until as local days YYYY-MM-DD (until is the last day included), tz the local zone they are judged in, chronological whether the surface is newest first by writing time (profile threads and replies tabs; not reposts, media, feeds or search). start is resumed progress. expected: shown ids in order, stop_reason, pages_fetched, pending (received, not shown, kept for the next handle), window {complete, undated}, exit code. A failure after records keeps them.

scenarios.name: newest-first-window-closes
scenarios.fact: On a chronological surface the window closes on a page wholly older than --since, ignoring pinned posts, provided every group so far was newest first. A group's time is its newest post. Posts outside the window are left out, pinned or not.

scenarios.name: local-day-boundaries-seoul
scenarios.fact: --since and --until are local days and --until is included: in Asia/Seoul, 2026-10-05..2026-10-07 is 2026-10-04T15:00:00Z up to but not including 2026-10-07T15:00:00Z.

scenarios.name: local-day-boundaries-utc
scenarios.fact: The same days judged in UTC keep different posts.

scenarios.name: order-break-in-page-never-closes
scenarios.fact: Once groups are out of newest-first order, no later page proves the window's start was passed: reading goes on to the end.

scenarios.name: order-break-across-pages
scenarios.fact: A page whose first group is newer than the previous page's last group also breaks the order.

scenarios.name: undated-counted-tombstone-not
scenarios.fact: A post without a date cannot be placed in a window: it is left out and counted once. A tombstone is not a post to place and is not counted.

scenarios.name: undated-group-stops-proof
scenarios.fact: On a chronological surface an undated group makes the order unknown, so the window cannot close.

scenarios.name: group-time-is-its-newest-post
scenarios.fact: A unit whose root is old but whose reply is recent is recent: it neither closes the window nor hides the recent reply.

scenarios.name: not-chronological-never-closes
scenarios.fact: A surface not ordered by writing time (reposts, media, feeds, search) cannot close a window: an old page does not mean older posts are done.

scenarios.name: window-open-at-limit
scenarios.fact: Stopping at --limit leaves the window open; the next handle continues.

scenarios.name: server-order-and-dedupe
scenarios.fact: Records keep the server's order; an id already shown is not shown again on a later page.

scenarios.name: limit-keeps-unshown-tail
scenarios.fact: Records received beyond --limit are kept for the next handle, not dropped and not re-requested.

scenarios.name: resume-tail-then-end
scenarios.fact: A resumed read shows the kept tail first, then requests from the saved cursor.

scenarios.name: repeated-cursor
scenarios.fact: A cursor already followed is a loop, not more data: reading stops before following it again. The page that repeated it is still shown (its records are new data); only the continuation is refused.

scenarios.name: failure-before-records
scenarios.fact: A request that fails before any record is read exits 6.

scenarios.name: failure-after-records
scenarios.fact: A failure after records keeps them: partial result, exit 8.

scenarios.name: block-after-records
scenarios.fact: A block stops the read with exit 5 even after records; the records stay in the result.

scenarios.name: login-after-records
scenarios.fact: A login stop exits 4 even after records; it is a failed read (error login), not a block: a block needs a person to clear it, a login needs a person to log in.

scenarios.name: budget-stop-resumes
scenarios.fact: Spending --max-requests is a resumable stop: the records so far, a next handle, exit 0 (output contract).

scenarios.name: explicit-empty
scenarios.fact: An explicitly empty surface is exit 7.

scenarios.name: capped-sample
scenarios.fact: A capped surface stops as server_capped even when --limit cut it; the unshown part of the sample is kept.

scenarios.name: single-batch-empty
scenarios.fact: An empty single batch is an explicit empty result.

profile_access.fact: An empty profile tab of a private profile the viewer does not follow is unavailable (exit 9): the reader cannot see it, which is not the same as it being empty. A private profile the viewer follows, or a public one, with an empty tab is an explicit empty result (exit 7).

exit_priority.fact: When several outcomes apply to one command, the exit code follows: blocked (5) > login (4) > target unavailable (9) > other failures (6, or 8 after records). A tombstone inside a list is a record marker, never exit 9.
